name: Direct Illumination Rendering with Gaussian Surfels
definition: A rendering method for direct illumination using Gaussian surfels, where outgoing radiance is a weighted average of incident radiance from light sources over the kernel's local support P, using a kernel κ (e.g., Gaussian, Uniform, Dirac delta).
summary: Direct Illumination Rendering with Gaussian Surfels computes outgoing radiance under direct light only, ignoring inter-reflections to enable non-recursive, direct evaluation without iterative solvers.
